title: Authentic Lebanese Tabouli Salad
description: A traditional Levantine herb salad loaded with fresh flat-leaf parsley, mint, bulgur wheat, tomatoes, and a zesty lemon-olive oil dressing.

ingredients.name: water, warm, for soaking the bulgur

instructions.text: Soak bulgur wheat in warm water for 15 minutes until softened, then drain thoroughly.
In a large bowl, mix finely chopped parsley, mint, tomatoes, and green onion.
Add soaked bulgur wheat to the salad mixture.
Drizzle extra virgin olive oil and lemon juice, season with salt and pepper, and toss gently.

title: Avocado and Citrus Salad with Toasted Seeds
description: A vibrant fresh salad combining sliced orange segments, creamy avocado, mixed greens, and pumpkin seeds.

instructions.text: Arrange mixed baby greens on plates.
Top with orange segments and avocado slices.
Sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds over salad.
Whisk olive oil, orange juice, salt, and pepper; drizzle over top.

title: Baingan Bharta with Brown Rice
description: Smoky roasted eggplant mashed into a tomato-onion masala and served with nutty brown rice.

instructions.text: Prick the eggplant all over and roast over a gas flame or under a hot grill, turning often, until the skin is charred and the flesh is completely soft. Cool, peel, and mash.
Rinse and cook brown rice according to package directions.
Heat oil in a pan. Cook onion until soft and golden, then add garlic, ginger, cumin, and coriander.
Add tomatoes and cook until saucy. Stir in mashed eggplant and salt; cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring to blend the smoky flesh with the masala.
Finish with cilantro and serve with brown rice.

nutrition.micronutrientEstimateSource: Approximate per-serving estimates from generic eggplant, brown rice, tomato, and onion composition; eggplant size and rice yield vary.

title: Baked Eggplant Parmigiana (Light Style)
description: A lighter Italian bake made with layered grilled eggplant, marinara tomato sauce, fresh basil, and melted skim mozzarella.

instructions.text: Brush eggplant slices lightly with olive oil and grill/bake at 200°C for 15 minutes until soft.
In a baking dish, spread a thin layer of marinara sauce, followed by grilled eggplant slices.
Top with fresh basil and shredded mozzarella; repeat layers.
Finish with parmesan cheese and bake at 190°C (375°F) for 25 minutes until bubbly.

imageAttribution.title: Baked Eggplant with tomato sauce and parmesan cheese
imageAttribution.creator: avlxyz

title: Brazilian Black Bean Stew (Light Feijoada)
description: A lighter vegetarian adaptation of Brazil’s national stew made with black beans, smoked paprika, sweet potatoes, and orange zest.

instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a pressure cooker; sauté onion, garlic, and sweet potato for 4 minutes.
Add soaked black beans, smoked paprika, bay leaf, orange peel, salt, and 4 cups water.
Pressure cook for 25 minutes until beans are tender and creamy.
Discard bay leaf and orange peel before serving.

title: Caprese Whole Wheat Wrap
description: A fresh Italian wrap packed with fresh mozzarella, ripe sliced tomatoes, basil leaves, and a touch of balsamic glaze.

instructions.text: Lay whole wheat tortillas flat on a clean board.
Arrange fresh mozzarella slices, tomato slices, and fresh basil leaves down the center.
Drizzle with extra virgin olive oil and balsamic glaze; sprinkle salt and pepper.
Roll wraps tightly, slice diagonally, and serve immediately.

title: Chakwi (Tripuri Boiled Vegetable Dish)
description: A traditional, oil-free Tripuri stew prepared with bamboo shoots, green papaya, jackfruit seeds, and baking soda.

instructions.text: Boil bamboo shoots, green papaya, jackfruit seeds, and green chillies in water with salt.
Add baking soda to soften ingredients and develop traditional aroma.
Simmer for 15 minutes until vegetables are completely cooked.
Stir in rice flour slurry to thicken gravy slightly and serve hot.

title: Chana Masala
description: A homestyle Punjabi chickpea curry simmered with tomatoes, ginger, amchur, and warming spices.

instructions.text: Soak chickpeas overnight, drain, and pressure-cook in fresh water until tender. Reserve some cooking liquid.
Heat oil in a pan and cook the onion until golden. Add ginger and garlic and stir for 1 minute.
Add cumin, coriander, and chana masala powder. Stir briefly, then add tomatoes and cook until they break down into a thick masala.
Add chickpeas, amchur, salt, and enough reserved liquid to make a thick curry. Simmer for 15 minutes, lightly mashing a few chickpeas to thicken.
Finish with lemon juice and cilantro. Serve hot with rice or whole-grain flatbread.

nutrition.micronutrientEstimateSource: Approximate per-serving estimates from generic cooked chickpeas, tomatoes, and spices; chickpea yield and salt use vary.

title: Chhena Poda (Light Baked Cottage Cheese Dessert)
description: A healthy version of Odisha's famous baked cottage cheese dessert made with low-fat paneer, jaggery, and cardamom.

instructions.text: Knead crumbled chhena with jaggery powder, semolina, and cardamom powder until soft.
Mix in crushed cashews and raisins.
Transfer mixture into a ghee-greased baking dish or cake tin.
Bake at 180°C for 30–35 minutes until the top turns golden brown and caramelized.

title: Chicken Potato Soup
description: A savory, light soup consisting of pressure-cooked chicken and potatoes blended together with shredded chicken pieces and herbs.

instructions.text: Pressure cook chicken pieces and potatoes with water until tender.
Remove potatoes, mash/grate them smoothly; remove chicken, debone, and shred finely.
Combine shredded chicken and grated potatoes in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, adding salt, pepper powder, and the Maggi cube.
Garnish with coriander or celery and serve piping hot.

title: Chilean Tomato and Onion Salad (Ensalada Chilena)
description: A staple Chilean side dish combining thinly sliced tomatoes, rinsed red onions, cilantro, and lemon-olive oil dressing.

ingredients.name: red onion, thinly sliced and rinsed in cold water
water, cold, for soaking the onion

instructions.text: Slice red onion thinly and soak in cold salted water for 10 minutes to remove harshness; drain.
Arrange sliced ripe tomatoes on a plate and top with drained onions.
Sprinkle fresh cilantro over salad.
Drizzle olive oil and lemon juice, season with salt and pepper, and serve.

title: Chilled Cucumber Avocado Soup
description: A creamy, raw blender soup made from fresh cucumbers, avocados, lime juice, cilantro, and garlic.

instructions.text: Combine cucumbers, avocado, water, lime juice, cilantro, garlic, salt, and pepper in a blender.
Blend on high speed until completely smooth.
Adjust salt or lime juice to taste.
Chill in refrigerator for 1 hour before serving cold.

title: Chinese Steamed Tofu with Garlic Soy Dressing
description: Silken tofu steamed to warm perfection and dressed with minced garlic, ginger, low-sodium soy sauce, and sesame oil.

instructions.text: Place block of silken tofu on a heatproof plate.
Steam over boiling water in a steamer for 8 minutes until warm.
Carefully drain off excess water surrounding tofu.
Mix tamari, sesame oil, garlic, and ginger; pour over warm tofu and garnish with spring onions.

imageAttribution.title: Chinese Steamed Tofu With Garlic Soy Dressing
imageAttribution.creator: Unsplash

title: Cholar Dal with Coconut (Bengali Gram Dal)
description: A traditional Bengali chana dal curry flavored with coconut slices, ginger, cumin, and dry red chillies.

instructions.text: Boil chana dal with turmeric, salt, and water until cooked but holding shape.
Heat mustard oil in a pan and fry coconut slices until golden; remove and set aside.
In the same oil, add cumin seeds, bay leaf, and ginger paste.
Pour in cooked dal, simmer for 10 minutes, stir in fried coconut, and serve.

title: Classic French Onion Soup (Light Version)
description: Rich, deeply caramelized onions simmered in savory broth, topped with a whole wheat crostini and melted Swiss cheese.

instructions.text: Cook sliced onions in olive oil on low heat for 30 minutes until deep golden brown.
Add garlic and broth; simmer for 15 minutes and season with salt and pepper.
Ladle soup into oven-safe bowls; top each with a baguette slice and cheese.
Broil in oven for 3 minutes until cheese is melted and bubbling.

title: Classic Italian Minestrone Soup
description: A hearty Tuscan vegetable soup packed with kidney beans, zucchini, tomatoes, and whole wheat pasta simmered in an aromatic herb broth.

instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a deep pot and sauté onion, carrots, celery, and garlic for 5 minutes.
Add zucchini, diced tomatoes, kidney beans, vegetable broth, and herbs.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add whole wheat pasta and cook for another 10 minutes until pasta is al dente.

title: Classic Mexican Guacamole with Veggie Sticks
description: Creamy mashed ripe avocados blended with lime juice, cilantro, tomatoes, onions, and jalapenos.

ingredients.name: carrot and cucumber sticks, for serving

instructions.text: Cut avocados in half, remove pits, and scoop flesh into a bowl.
Mash avocados coarsely with a fork; stir in lime juice and salt immediately.
Fold in diced red onion, tomato, jalapeno, and chopped cilantro.
Serve fresh with carrot and cucumber sticks.

title: Cucumber Soup
description: A refreshing, blended soup made with sautéed cucumbers, potatoes, garlic, and onions, thickened slightly with cornflour and cream.

instructions.text: Heat ghee/oil in a pan, add crushed garlic, and stir-fry until golden brown.
Add chopped onions and sauté until light pink.
Add cucumbers and potatoes; stir-fry until moisture evaporates.
Stir in cornflour and sauté for 2-3 minutes.
Add boiling water, cover, and cook until tender; let cool and blend smoothly.
Bring back to a boil with Maggi cubes and serve hot garnished with fresh cream.

title: Dal Khichdi
description: A comfort dish cooked by simmering yellow moong dal and rice together with mild spices, turmeric, and ghee.

instructions.text: Wash moong dal and rice together thoroughly.
Heat ghee in a pressure cooker; add cumin seeds and asafoetida.
Add washed dal, rice, turmeric, salt, and water.
Pressure cook for 4-5 whistles until soft and porridge-like.
Drizzle a small spoonful of ghee before serving hot.

title: Dalma (Odisha Lentil and Vegetable Stew)
description: A wholesome Odia stew cooked with split yellow lentils, raw papaya, pumpkin, eggplant, and dry roasted spices.

instructions.text: Pressure cook toor dal with raw papaya, pumpkin, eggplant, taro, turmeric, salt, and water until tender.
Heat oil/ghee in a small pan, add mustard seeds and cumin seeds until they splutter.
Pour tempering into boiled dal-vegetable stew.
Sprinkle freshly roasted bhaja masala on top and mix well before serving.

title: Dudhi Muthia (Gujarati Steamed Bottle Gourd Dumplings)
description: Nutritious steamed Gujarati dumplings made with grated bottle gourd, whole wheat flour, and fragrant spices.

instructions.text: Squeeze slight excess water from grated dudhi and combine with wheat flour, besan, turmeric, green chilli paste, and salt.
Knead gently into a soft dough without adding extra water.
Shape into cylindrical logs and steam in a steamer for 18–20 minutes.
Slice logs into rounds and sauté lightly with mustard seeds and sesame seeds.

title: Eastern European Beetroot Borscht
description: A vibrant ruby-red beet soup cooked with cabbage, carrots, potatoes, and dill, served with a dollop of fresh yogurt.

instructions.text: Sauté onion and carrot in a pot with a drop of oil for 4 minutes.
Add grated beets, diced potato, shredded cabbage, and vegetable broth.
Simmer for 25 minutes until all vegetables are soft.
Stir in lemon juice and dill; serve hot with a spoonful of Greek yogurt.

title: Egyptian Ful Medames (Spiced Fava Beans)
description: A traditional Egyptian breakfast dish of slow-cooked fava beans seasoned with garlic, cumin, lemon juice, and olive oil.

instructions.text: Warm cooked fava beans in a pot with 3 tbsp water.
Slightly mash beans with a fork or potato masher.
Stir in minced garlic, cumin powder, lemon juice, and salt.
Transfer to a bowl, drizzle generously with extra virgin olive oil, and garnish with parsley.

title: Ethiopian Lentil Stew (Misir Wot)
description: A spicy Ethiopian red lentil stew simmered with berbere spice blend, garlic, ginger, and tomatoes.

instructions.text: Sauté chopped onions in olive oil on medium heat for 8 minutes until golden.
Add garlic, ginger, and berbere spice blend; stir for 1 minute.
Add tomato paste, red lentils, water, and salt.
Simmer covered for 20–25 minutes until lentils are soft and thick.

title: Foxtail Millet Vegetable Upma
description: A savory South Indian millet breakfast with vegetables, ginger, curry leaves, and toasted cashews.

instructions.text: Rinse the millet and drain. Dry-toast it in a pan for 3 minutes, stirring, then set aside.
Heat oil in the pan. Add mustard seeds and cashews; when the seeds pop and cashews turn golden, add curry leaves, ginger, and onion.
Add carrot, beans, peas, water, and salt. Bring to a boil, then stir in the millet.
Cover and cook on low until the millet is tender and liquid is absorbed, about 15 to 20 minutes. Rest for 5 minutes, fluff, and finish with lemon juice.

nutrition.micronutrientEstimateSource: Approximate per-serving estimates from generic millet, vegetable, and cashew composition; millet type and produce size vary.

title: French Ratatouille
description: A classic Provençal vegetable stew made of layered zucchini, eggplant, bell peppers, tomatoes, garlic, and fresh herbs.

instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a heavy pot; sauté onion and garlic for 3 minutes.
Add bell peppers, eggplant, and zucchini; cook for 8 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and Herbes de Provence; season with salt.
Simmer covered on low heat for 20 minutes until vegetables are meltingly tender.

title: German Cucumber and Dill Salad (Gurkensalat)
description: Thinly sliced cucumbers tossed in a light, refreshing dressing of sour cream or Greek yogurt, vinegar, and fresh dill.

ingredients.name: Greek yogurt or light sour cream

instructions.text: Toss sliced cucumbers with salt and let drain in a colander for 15 minutes.
Whisk Greek yogurt, white vinegar, honey, dill, and white pepper in a bowl.
Gently pat cucumbers dry with a towel.
Toss cucumbers in dill dressing and chill before serving.

title: Global Quinoa Edamame Power Bowl
description: A nutrient-packed protein bowl featuring fluffy quinoa, steamed edamame, shredded purple cabbage, carrots, and sesame dressing.

instructions.text: Arrange cooked quinoa in bowls as the base.
Top with sections of steamed edamame, purple cabbage, and shredded carrot.
Whisk sesame oil, soy sauce, and lime juice.
Drizzle dressing over power bowl before serving.

title: Greek Baked Giant Beans (Gigantes Plaki)
description: Large butter beans baked slow in a rich, oregano-infused tomato and garlic sauce topped with fresh parsley.

ingredients.name: cooked butter beans or lima beans

instructions.text: Sauté onion and garlic in olive oil until soft.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, salt, pepper, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Mix in cooked butter beans and transfer to a baking dish.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 30 minutes until sauce thickens.

title: Greek Mediterranean Quinoa Salad
description: A vibrant, refreshing Mediterranean bowl combining protein-rich quinoa, cucumbers, cherry tomatoes, Kalamata olives, and crumbled feta cheese with extra virgin olive oil.

instructions.text: Cook quinoa in water/stock for 15 minutes until fluffy; let cool.
In a large bowl, combine cooled quinoa, tomatoes, cucumber, Kalamata olives, and crumbled feta.
Whisk extra virgin olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, salt, and pepper in a small jar.
Pour dressing over salad, toss gently, and serve chilled.

imageAttribution.title: Quinoa salad
imageAttribution.creator: Geoff Peters from Vancouver, BC, Canada

title: Grilled Chicken Fajita Salad
description: Sizzling grilled chicken breast strips tossed with sautéed bell peppers, onions, romaine lettuce, and salsa.

instructions.text: Toss chicken strips, bell peppers, and onion with taco seasoning and olive oil.
Grill chicken on a skillet over medium-high heat until cooked through.
Sauté peppers and onions until tender crisp.
Serve chicken and veggies over a bed of chopped romaine lettuce with salsa.

title: Grilled Lemon Herb Asparagus
description: Fresh tender asparagus spears grilled with olive oil, garlic, lemon zest, and cracked black pepper.

instructions.text: Snap off woody ends of asparagus spears.
Toss spears with olive oil, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.
Grill on a hot skillet or grill pan for 5–7 minutes, turning occasionally.
Transfer to plate, sprinkle lemon zest, and squeeze fresh lemon juice.

imageAttribution.title: Grilled asparagus with fresh lemon and olives
imageAttribution.creator: Shoshanah

title: Healthy Chia Seed Pudding with Berries
description: A gut-friendly nutrient pot made from chia seeds soaked in almond milk, topped with fresh berries and cinnamon.

instructions.text: Whisk chia seeds, almond milk, vanilla extract, and maple syrup in a jar.
Let sit for 10 minutes, whisk again to break lumps, and refrigerate for 4 hours or overnight.
Scoop into serving cups.
Top with fresh berries and a pinch of cinnamon.

title: Hearty Golden Lentil and Spinach Soup
description: A nourishing golden soup cooked with yellow lentils, turmeric, ginger, fresh spinach, and lemon juice.

instructions.text: Sauté onion and ginger in olive oil for 3 minutes.
Add turmeric powder, yellow lentils, and vegetable broth; bring to a boil.
Simmer covered for 20 minutes until lentils break down.
Stir in fresh spinach and lemon juice; cook for 2 minutes and serve.

title: Himachali Siddu (Steamed Whole Wheat Stuffed Bun)
description: A traditional Himachali steamed bread made from whole wheat dough stuffed with a spiced poppy seed and walnut filling.

ingredients.name: poppy seeds (khus khus), soaked and ground

instructions.text: Knead wheat flour with warm water, yeast, and salt into a soft dough; leave to ferment for 2 hours.
Prepare stuffing by mixing ground poppy seeds, walnuts, chillies, ginger, and salt.
Flatten fermented dough portions, fill with poppy seed mixture, fold into half-moon shapes, and seal edges.
Steam in a steamer for 15–20 minutes and serve warm with dal or chutney.

title: Indonesian Gado-Gado Salad
description: A traditional Indonesian salad of blanched vegetables, hard-boiled eggs, and tofu served with a light peanut dressing.

instructions.text: Arrange blanched cabbage, green beans, bean sprouts, pan-seared tofu, and hard-boiled eggs on a platter.
Whisk peanut butter, lime juice, soy sauce, and warm water until smooth.
Pour peanut dressing over arranged vegetables and tofu.
Serve at room temperature.

title: Israeli Couscous Salad with Roasted Vegetables
description: Pearl couscous tossed with oven-roasted zucchini, bell peppers, cherry tomatoes, and a herb-lemon vinaigrette.

instructions.text: Toss zucchini, bell pepper, and tomatoes in 1 tbsp olive oil; roast at 200°C for 20 minutes.
Cook pearl couscous in boiling water for 8 minutes; drain.
Combine roasted vegetables and couscous in a bowl.
Dress with remaining olive oil, lemon juice, parsley, salt, and pepper.

title: Italian Herb Baked Zucchini Boats
description: Halved zucchini hollowed and stuffed with diced vegetables, marinara sauce, and baked with a sprinkle of parmesan.

instructions.text: Scoop out flesh from halved zucchini to create hollow boats.
Chop scooped flesh and sauté with bell peppers, Italian seasoning, and olive oil.
Mix in marinara sauce and spoon back into zucchini boats.
Top with parmesan cheese and bake at 190°C (375°F) for 20 minutes.

title: Italian Roasted Garlic and Tomato Bruschetta
description: Toasted whole grain bread rubbed with garlic and topped with fresh diced tomatoes, basil, and extra virgin olive oil.

instructions.text: Toast whole grain bread slices until crisp.
Rub one side of toasted bread with halved garlic clove.
Mix diced tomatoes, minced garlic, basil, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spoon tomato mixture onto toasted bread and drizzle with balsamic glaze.

title: Japanese Miso Soup with Tofu and Wakame
description: A light, gut-friendly fermented dashi broth featuring silken tofu, wakame seaweed, and spring onions.

ingredients.name: water, warm, for soaking the wakame

instructions.text: Soak dried wakame seaweed in warm water for 5 minutes to rehydrate.
Heat kombu dashi broth in a saucepan until hot (do not boil).
Ladle out a little warm broth into a cup, add miso paste, and whisk until smooth.
Add tofu and wakame to pot, stir in dissolved miso paste, turn off heat, and serve topped with spring onions.

imageAttribution.title: Miso soup with tofu and seaweed
imageAttribution.creator: Ocdp

title: Japanese Sesame Cucumber Salad (Sunomono)
description: Crisp Japanese cucumber ribbons pickled gently in rice vinegar, soy sauce, and toasted sesame seeds.

ingredients.name: Japanese or Persian cucumbers, thinly sliced

instructions.text: Toss sliced cucumbers with a pinch of salt and let sit for 10 minutes; squeeze out excess water.
Whisk rice vinegar, soy sauce, and maple syrup in a small bowl.
Pour vinegar dressing over drained cucumbers.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and serve chilled.

title: Kadi Patta Paneer Sauté (Curry Leaf Cottage Cheese)
description: Cubes of low-fat cottage cheese tossed with fresh curry leaves, turmeric, and cracked black pepper.

instructions.text: Heat sesame oil in a skillet and add fresh curry leaves until fragrant and crisp.
Stir in green chilli paste, turmeric powder, and salt.
Add paneer cubes and sauté gently on medium heat for 5 minutes.
Finish with crushed black pepper and serve hot.

title: Kalan (Kerala Yoghurt Plantain Curry)
description: A traditional Kerala Sadya dish featuring raw plantain cooked in thick yoghurt, coconut, and fenugreek tempering.

ingredients.name: fresh grated coconut (ground with the cumin and green chillies)
cumin seeds, ground with the coconut
green chillies, ground with the coconut

instructions.text: Boil raw plantain cubes with turmeric powder, salt, and water until tender.
Add ground coconut-cumin paste and simmer for 5 minutes.
Lower heat, stir in whisked sour curd, and simmer gently until thickened.
Temper with mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, and curry leaves in coconut oil.

title: Kangshoi (Manipuri Oil-Free Vegetable Stew)
description: An oil-free Manipuri stew cooked with seasonal vegetables, fermented fish or beans, maroi leaves, and ginger.

instructions.text: Boil 3 cups of water in a deep pot with sliced ginger, slit chillies, and fermented soybean.
Add green peas/beans and cook for 8 minutes.
Add leafy greens and salt; simmer uncovered for 5–7 minutes until tender.
Serve piping hot as a clear nutritious broth.

title: Kanjeevaram Idli (Spiced Steamed Rice Cakes)
description: A fragrant South Indian steamed cake spiced with black pepper, cumin, ginger, and curry leaves.

ingredients.name: idli rice, soaked and coarsely ground
urad dal, soaked and ground smooth

instructions.text: Mix ground rice and urad dal batter; ferment overnight.
Add crushed black pepper, cumin seeds, chopped ginger, sesame oil, curry leaves, and salt.
Pour batter into greased idli molds or leaf lined containers.
Steam for 15 minutes until fully set and serve with tomato chutney.

title: Kanji (Odia Rice and Curd Fermented Soup)
description: A cooling, probiotic Odia rice water soup fermented overnight with mustard paste, curd, and vegetables.

instructions.text: Combine rice water, whisked sour curd, mustard paste, and salt; leave covered for 6 hours to ferment.
Add boiled drumsticks and pumpkin pieces to the fermented mixture.
Bring the mixture to a gentle boil on low heat.
Temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves in hot oil and serve warm.

title: Kashmiri Haak Saag (Steamed Collard Greens)
description: A minimalist Kashmiri specialty featuring collard greens cooked gently with mustard oil, asafoetida, and dry red chillies.

ingredients.name: collard greens (haak) or spinach, thoroughly cleaned

instructions.text: Heat mustard oil in a heavy pot until smoking point; cool slightly.
Add asafoetida and dry red chillies.
Add whole green leaves, water, salt, and fennel powder.
Simmer uncovered on medium heat for 12–15 minutes until leaves are tender yet bright green.

title: Kenyan Sukuma Wiki (Sautéed Collard Greens)
description: An East African staple dish of collard greens braised with tomatoes, onions, cumin, and lemon.

instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a pan; sauté onion for 4 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes and cumin; cook for 3 minutes.
Add chopped collard greens and 2 tbsp water; cover and cook for 8 minutes.
Finish with lemon juice, salt, and pepper.

title: Kerala Cabbage Thoran
description: A quick Kerala-style cabbage stir-fry with coconut, mustard seeds, curry leaves, and green chilli.

instructions.text: Mix the cabbage with coconut, shallots, chilli, cumin, and salt.
Heat oil in a covered skillet. Add mustard seeds and curry leaves; let the seeds pop.
Add the cabbage mixture and water. Cover and cook over low heat for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring once or twice, until just tender but not mushy.
Uncover and cook briefly to evaporate excess moisture. Taste and serve as a vegetable side with rice and dal.

nutrition.micronutrientEstimateSource: Approximate per-serving estimates from generic cabbage and coconut composition; coconut amount and salt use vary.

title: Kerala Coconut Fish Curry
description: A coastal-style fish curry with coconut milk, tomato, tamarind, curry leaves, and black mustard seeds.

instructions.text: Cut the fish into large pieces and season lightly with salt and turmeric.
Heat oil in a wide pan. Add mustard seeds and curry leaves; when fragrant, add shallots, ginger, and garlic and cook until softened.
Stir in chilli powder and tomatoes. Cook until the tomatoes soften, then add coconut milk, tamarind, and 120 ml water. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Slide in the fish and simmer gently until opaque and just cooked through, about 7 to 10 minutes depending on thickness. Avoid vigorous stirring; taste and adjust salt.

nutrition.micronutrientEstimateSource: Approximate per-serving estimates from generic white fish, light coconut milk, and vegetables; fish species and coconut milk brands vary.

title: Khandvi (Gujarati Savory Gram Flour Rolls)
description: A classic Gujarati steamed snack made from gram flour and buttermilk, tempered with mustard seeds and curry leaves.

instructions.text: Whisk besan, buttermilk, turmeric, ginger-chilli paste, and salt into a smooth, lump-free batter.
Cook the mixture in a heavy pan on low flame, stirring continuously until thick and glossy.
Spread thinly onto the back of greased stainless steel plates while hot.
Allow to cool, cut into strips, roll tightly, and temper with mustard seeds, curry leaves, and sesame seeds in hot oil.

title: Kordoi / Assamese Whole Wheat Savory Snacks
description: A traditional Assamese tea-time snack shaped like starfruit (kordoi), made healthy using whole wheat flour and carom seeds.

instructions.text: Knead whole wheat flour, ajwain, kalonji, salt, mustard oil, and water into a firm dough.
Divide into small balls, roll into flat ovals, and make parallel vertical slits leaving edges intact.
Roll tightly from side to side to form the starfruit (kordoi) shape.
Air-fry at 180°C or bake until golden crisp and serve warm.

title: Korean Kimchi Fried Brown Rice
description: A flavorful Korean bowl featuring gut-healthy fermented kimchi stir-fried with brown rice, sesame oil, and a fried egg.

instructions.text: Heat sesame oil in a skillet; sauté garlic and chopped kimchi for 3 minutes.
Add cold brown rice, kimchi juice, and soy sauce, breaking up rice clumps over high heat.
Stir-fry for 4 minutes until rice absorbs flavors.
Divide into bowls, top each with a pan-fried egg, spring onions, and sesame seeds.

title: Kothimbir Vadi (Maharashtrian Steamed Coriander Cakes)
description: Crispy savory cakes made from fresh coriander leaves and gram flour batter, steamed and lightly pan-sautéed.

ingredients.name: packed fresh coriander leaves, finely chopped

instructions.text: Mix chopped coriander, besan, rice flour, green chilli-ginger paste, sesame seeds, turmeric, and salt into a thick dough.
Shape into a cylindrical roll and steam in a steamer for 15 minutes.
Allow to cool completely and slice into 1/2-inch thick cakes.
Pan-sauté sliced vadis in a tablespoon of oil until outer surfaces are crisp.

title: Kotte Kadubu (Karnataka Jackfruit Leaf Steamed Cakes)
description: A Karnataka coastal delicacy made of ground rice and urad dal batter steamed inside woven jackfruit leaves.

ingredients.name: woven jackfruit leaf baskets or banana leaf cups

instructions.text: Grind soaked urad dal and rice separately into a smooth batter; mix and ferment overnight.
Add salt to fermented batter and pour into clean jackfruit leaf baskets.
Steam in a steamer or idli cooker for 15–20 minutes.
Unwrap steaming hot kadubu and serve with coconut chutney or sambar.

title: Lebanese Baba Ganoush (Eggplant Dip)
description: Smoky roasted eggplant dip blended with tahini, garlic, lemon juice, and extra virgin olive oil.

instructions.text: Prick eggplant with a fork and roast whole at 220°C for 40 minutes until collapsed and charred.
Scoop out soft inner flesh and drain excess liquid.
Mash flesh with tahini, garlic, lemon juice, and salt until creamy.
Drizzle olive oil and sprinkle parsley before serving.

title: Lemon Herb Chicken
description: Bright, protein-rich chicken with herbs and lemon for an easy weeknight meal.

instructions.text: Season the chicken with lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, oregano, and herbs.
Marinate for 15 minutes while the oven preheats to 220 degrees Celsius.
Roast or pan-sear until golden and the thickest part reaches 74 degrees Celsius.
Finish with extra lemon zest and serve immediately.

nutrition.micronutrientEstimateSource: Approximate estimate based on USDA FoodData Central generic chicken breast (FDC 171077) and listed recipe measures; household conversions are approximate, and herbs, seasoning, and cooking retention are not fully modeled.

title: Light Baked Fish Tacos
description: Warm corn tortillas stuffed with baked spiced white fish, shredded cabbage slaw, fresh cilantro, and lime.

instructions.text: Season fish fillets with chilli powder, cumin, and salt; bake at 200°C for 12 minutes.
Toss shredded purple cabbage with lime juice and cilantro to make slaw.
Warm corn tortillas on a dry tawa/skillet.
Flake baked fish into tortillas and top with cabbage slaw.

title: Madra / Himachali Chickpea Yogurt Curry
description: A rich Himachali slow-cooked chickpea curry prepared in fresh curd and tempered with whole aromatic spices.

instructions.text: Heat ghee in a pan and add cumin seeds, cloves, cardamom, and cinnamon.
Add whisked curd on low flame, stirring continuously in one direction to prevent curdling.
Add turmeric, coriander powder, salt, and boiled chickpeas.
Simmer on low heat for 15 minutes until gravy turns thick and aromatic.

title: Masoor Dal with Spinach
description: A weeknight red lentil dal with spinach, tomato, cumin, and a fragrant garlic tempering.

instructions.text: Rinse lentils until the water runs mostly clear. Add them to a pot with water, turmeric, tomatoes, and salt.
Bring to a boil, skim any foam, then simmer partly covered until the lentils are soft, about 20 minutes. Add water if needed.
Stir in spinach and cook until wilted. In a small pan, heat oil, add cumin seeds and sliced garlic, and cook until fragrant and just golden.
Pour the garlic tempering into the dal. Stir in lemon juice, adjust salt, and serve with rice or millet.

nutrition.micronutrientEstimateSource: Approximate per-serving estimates from generic cooked lentils, spinach, and vegetables; lentil yield and salt use vary.

title: Mediterranean Chickpea Tuna Salad (Egg-Free)
description: A high-protein salad blending flaked light tuna, chickpeas, diced celery, red onion, and lemon-herb olive oil.

ingredients.name: canned light tuna in water, drained

instructions.text: Flake drained tuna into a bowl with a fork.
Add chickpeas, diced celery, red onion, and chopped parsley.
Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper; pour over salad.
Toss gently and serve over greens or in wraps.

title: Menthya Matvadi Palya (Karnataka Fenugreek Lentil Stir-Fry)
description: A nutrient-dense Karnataka dry dish made with fresh fenugreek leaves and coarsely ground steamed lentils.

instructions.text: Coarsely blend soaked chana dal with green chillies and salt; steam the mixture for 10 minutes and crumble.
Heat coconut oil in a pan, add mustard seeds and turmeric powder.
Add chopped methi leaves and sauté until wilted.
Mix in crumbled steamed dal, cook for 5 minutes, finish with lemon juice, and serve.

title: Mexican Black Bean and Corn Bowl
description: A vibrant Southwestern bowl filled with black beans, sweet corn, diced avocado, cilantro, and lime dressing.

instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine drained black beans, sweet corn, diced bell pepper, red onion, and cilantro.
Whisk lime juice, olive oil, cumin, and salt.
Pour dressing over bean mixture and toss gently.
Fold in diced avocado just before serving.

title: Mexican Zucchini and Corn Sauté (Calabacitas)
description: A traditional Mexican vegetable side dish of sautéed zucchini, corn, tomatoes, garlic, and fresh herbs.

instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a skillet and sauté onion and garlic for 3 minutes.
Add diced zucchini and sweet corn, stir-frying for 5 minutes.
Add chopped tomato, salt, and pepper; cook for 3 minutes until tender.
Serve warm as a light side dish.

title: Middle Eastern Baked Falafel
description: Crispy baked patties made from ground chickpeas, fresh parsley, cilantro, and warm Middle Eastern spices.

instructions.text: Pulse soaked chickpeas, herbs, onion, garlic, cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper in a food processor into a coarse mixture.
Stir in baking soda and chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Form into small flattened patties and place on a parchment-lined baking tray.
Brush lightly with olive oil and bake at 200°C (400°F) for 20–25 minutes until golden brown.

title: Middle Eastern Freekeh Vegetable Pilaf
description: Nutty roasted green wheat (freekeh) cooked with onions, carrots, peas, and fragrant warm spices.

instructions.text: Sauté onion and carrot in olive oil for 4 minutes.
Add rinsed freekeh, cumin, and cinnamon; stir for 1 minute.
Pour in vegetable broth and salt; bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 20 minutes; stir in green peas and fluff with a fork.

title: Missi Roti (North Indian Spiced Chickpea Flatbread)
description: A nutrient-rich North Indian flatbread prepared by blending whole wheat flour and chickpea flour with aromatic spices.

instructions.text: Combine wheat flour, besan, minced onion, ajwain, coriander seeds, spices, and salt.
Knead into a firm dough adding water gradually.
Roll portions into round flatbreads and cook on a preheated tawa.
Flip and toast until lightly speckled brown on both sides.

title: Moong Dal Chilla
description: Savory North Indian split-moong pancakes with ginger, cumin, and cilantro for a protein-rich breakfast.

instructions.text: Rinse the moong dal and soak in plenty of water for at least 4 hours. Drain.
Blend the dal with the measured water, ginger, turmeric, and salt into a smooth, pourable batter. Stir in onion, chilli, cumin, and cilantro.
Heat a nonstick or seasoned skillet over medium heat and lightly oil it. Pour in a quarter of the batter and spread into a thin circle.
Cook until the edges release and the underside is golden, about 2 to 3 minutes. Flip and cook the other side; repeat with the remaining batter.

nutrition.micronutrientEstimateSource: Approximate per-serving estimates from generic ingredient composition and stated quantities; soaking, batter thickness, and salt use vary.

title: Moroccan Carrot and Cumin Salad
description: Tender cooked carrot coins tossed in a fragrant dressing of garlic, cumin, paprika, lemon juice, and cilantro.

instructions.text: Steam carrot coins for 6–8 minutes until tender crisp.
Heat olive oil in a small pan; sauté garlic, cumin, and paprika for 30 seconds.
Toss warm carrots in warm spiced oil mixture.
Add lemon juice, cilantro, and salt; serve warm or chilled.

title: Moroccan Vegetable Tagine
description: A fragrant North African slow-cooked stew of chickpeas, sweet potatoes, carrots, zucchini, dried apricots, and warm spices.

instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a deep pot or tagine and sauté onion for 3 minutes.
Add sweet potatoes, carrots, spices, and stir for 2 minutes to release aromatics.
Add chickpeas, dried apricots, and vegetable broth; cover and simmer for 25 minutes.
Stir in zucchini and cook for another 10 minutes until all vegetables are tender.

title: North African Spiced Roasted Cauliflower
description: Whole cauliflower florets roasted with ras el hanout spice blend, olive oil, and served with a lemon-tahini drizzle.

ingredients.name: ras el hanout or cumin/paprika blend

instructions.text: Toss cauliflower florets with olive oil, ras el hanout, and salt.
Roast at 200°C (400°F) for 25 minutes until edges are browned.
Whisk tahini, lemon juice, and warm water until smooth.
Drizzle tahini sauce over roasted cauliflower.

title: Olan (Kerala White Gourd and Cowpeas Curry)
description: A soothing, light Kerala curry made with ash gourd, red cowpeas, fresh coconut milk, and curry leaves.

instructions.text: Cook ash gourd cubes and green chillies in thin coconut milk with salt until soft.
Add boiled red cowpeas and simmer for 3 minutes.
Pour in thick coconut milk, add fresh curry leaves, and remove immediately from heat.
Drizzle raw coconut oil over the curry before serving.

title: Overnight Oats
description: Creamy oats with chia, berries, and vanilla for a quick fiber-rich breakfast.

instructions.text: Stir the oats, milk, chia seeds, yogurt, vanilla, and honey together.
Refrigerate overnight so the oats soften and absorb the liquid.
Top with berries in the morning and serve chilled.

nutrition.micronutrientEstimateSource: Approximate estimate based on USDA FoodData Central generic rolled oats and chia seed entries (FDC 2346396, 170554) plus generic estimates for other listed ingredients; household conversions, dairy brands, berries, and preparation vary.

imageAttribution.title: How to Make Bircher Muesli (Overnight Oats)
imageAttribution.creator: simpleprovisions

title: Palak Paneer
description: A lighter North Indian spinach and paneer curry with ginger, garlic, and a modest amount of creaminess from yogurt.

instructions.text: Blanch spinach in boiling water for 1 minute, transfer to cold water, drain, and blend to a smooth puree.
Warm half the oil in a pan and lightly brown the paneer on two sides. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil. Cook onion until soft, then add ginger, garlic, cumin, and tomato; cook until the tomato softens.
Stir in the spinach puree and garam masala and simmer gently for 5 minutes. Lower the heat, stir in yogurt, then fold in paneer and warm without boiling. Season and serve.

nutrition.micronutrientEstimateSource: Approximate per-serving estimates from generic spinach, paneer, and yogurt composition; paneer brands and cooking yield vary.

imageAttribution.title: Palak Paneer (Pureed Spinach with cottage cheese)
imageAttribution.creator: rovingI

title: Palak (Spinach) Soup
description: A smooth green soup made by simmering fresh spinach leaves with garlic, ginger, and subtle seasoning, finished with lemon juice.

instructions.text: Heat oil/ghee in a saucepan and sauté garlic, ginger, and onion until translucent.
Add fresh spinach leaves and sauté for 2-3 minutes until wilted.
Pour in stock/water and simmer for 3 minutes. Remove from heat and allow to cool.
Blend the mixture smoothly using a blender.
Return to saucepan, season with salt and pepper, bring to a gentle simmer, and finish with lemon juice.

title: Parsi Egg Akuri (Spiced Soft Scrambled Eggs)
description: A famous Parsi breakfast dish consisting of soft-scrambled eggs cooked with onions, tomatoes, green chillies, and cilantro.

instructions.text: Heat butter/oil in a pan and sauté onions and green chillies until soft.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, cumin powder, and salt; cook until soft.
Pour in beaten eggs and coriander; cook on low heat stirring constantly.
Remove from heat while eggs are still soft and creamy.

nutrition.micronutrientEstimateSource: Per-serving values from CTI_RECEIPES.pdf. Vitamin D converted from IU to mcg (1 mcg = 40 IU).

title: Persian Herb Salad (Sabzi Khordan)
description: A traditional Iranian platter of fresh mint, tarragon, radishes, walnuts, and feta cheese eaten as a light starter.

instructions.text: Wash and thoroughly dry all fresh herbs.
Arrange fresh herbs, sliced radishes, and spring onions on a platter.
Add crumbled feta cheese and walnut halves.
Serve fresh alongside whole grain bread.

title: Peruvian Quinoa Vegetable Soup
description: An Andean whole-grain soup loaded with quinoa, potatoes, carrots, zucchini, and traditional South American spices.

instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a pot and sauté onion and carrot for 4 minutes.
Add potatoes, rinsed quinoa, cumin, salt, and vegetable broth.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add zucchini and cook for another 5 minutes until quinoa and veggies are soft.

title: Polish Beetroot and Apple Salad
description: A crisp, colorful Polish salad combining shredded cooked beets, tart apples, lemon juice, and cold-pressed oil.

instructions.text: Grate cooked beets and tart green apple into a bowl.
Drizzle immediately with lemon juice to keep apple bright.
Add olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Toss well and let sit for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Pudina Chutney Stuffed Tandoori Fish
description: Whole fish fillets stuffed with fresh mint-coriander green chutney and roasted to tender perfection.

instructions.text: Blend mint, coriander, green chillies, lemon juice, cumin, and salt into a smooth green chutney.
Slit fish fillets horizontally to create a pocket and stuff with chutney.
Brush outer surface lightly with olive oil.
Grill in a preheated oven or pan-sear for 5–6 minutes per side until cooked through.

title: Ragi Dosa
description: Crisp, naturally gluten-free finger-millet dosas with yogurt-free batter and a gentle cumin tempering.

instructions.text: Whisk the ragi flour, rice flour, salt, and water until smooth. The batter should be thin and pourable; rest it for 15 minutes.
Stir in onion, cumin, chilli, and cilantro. Mix again before each dosa because the flour settles.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and wipe with a little oil. Pour a ladle of batter from the outside toward the center, leaving small holes for crisping.
Drizzle a little oil around the edge and cook until crisp and browned underneath. Fold and serve hot; repeat with the remaining batter.

nutrition.micronutrientEstimateSource: Approximate per-serving estimates from generic finger millet, rice flour, and vegetable composition; flour brands and oil use vary.

title: Rajma with Brown Rice
description: A balanced North Indian kidney bean curry served with fiber-rich brown rice and fresh cilantro.

instructions.text: Soak the kidney beans overnight, then drain. Pressure-cook in fresh water until completely tender, or simmer in a covered pot until soft.
Rinse the brown rice and cook in water according to the package directions until tender.
Heat oil in a pot. Cook the onion until golden, add ginger-garlic paste, then stir in cumin, coriander, turmeric, and garam masala.
Add the tomato puree and cook until thickened. Stir in the cooked beans and enough cooking liquid for a thick curry; simmer for 15 minutes and season to taste.
Serve the rajma over brown rice and finish with cilantro.

nutrition.micronutrientEstimateSource: Approximate per-serving estimates from generic cooked kidney beans, brown rice, and vegetables; bean variety, cooked yield, and salt use vary.

title: Rajma (Red Kidney Bean Curry)
description: A North Indian curry made with slow-cooked red kidney beans simmered in a spiced onion-tomato gravy.

instructions.text: Pressure cook soaked rajma in salted water until soft and tender.
Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds, and sauté onions until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, turmeric, chilli powder, and rajma masala; cook until oil separates.
Add boiled rajma along with its cooking liquid and simmer for 15 minutes.
Lightly mash a few beans to thicken gravy and serve hot with brown rice.

title: Roasted Butternut Squash and Sage Soup
description: Velvety smooth autumn soup prepared from oven-roasted butternut squash, garlic, onion, and fresh sage.

instructions.text: Toss squash cubes with olive oil; roast at 200°C for 30 minutes.
Sauté onion, garlic, and sage in a pot for 4 minutes.
Add roasted squash and vegetable broth; simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend until velvety smooth and season with nutmeg, salt, and pepper.

imageAttribution.title: Roasted Butternut Squash And Sage Soup
imageAttribution.creator: Unsplash

title: Sattu Paratha (Bihari Roasted Gram Flatbread)
description: A staple Bihari flatbread stuffed with spiced roasted Bengal gram flour (sattu), rich in plant protein and dietary fiber.

instructions.text: Prepare a smooth dough using whole wheat flour, water, and a pinch of salt.
In a bowl, mix sattu, chopped onions, chillies, mustard oil, pickle oil, lemon juice, coriander, and salt.
Stuff portions of sattu mixture into dough balls, seal, and roll gently into flatbreads.
Cook on a heated skillet (tawa) with minimal oil until golden spots appear on both sides.

title: Shakshuka (North African Poached Eggs in Tomato Sauce)
description: Gently poached eggs resting in a rich, spiced sauce of tomatoes, bell peppers, onions, garlic, and cumin.

instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a skillet; sauté onion, bell pepper, and garlic for 5 minutes.
Add cumin, paprika, crushed tomatoes, salt, and pepper; simmer for 10 minutes until sauce thickens.
Make 4 small wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each well.
Cover skillet and cook on low heat for 5–8 minutes until egg whites are set.

title: Sol Kadhi (Kokum and Coconut Milk Drink)
description: A cooling Goan-Konkani digestive drink made from natural kokum extract, fresh coconut milk, garlic, and chillies.

ingredients.name: dried kokum, soaked in warm water

instructions.text: Extract dark red kokum juice (amsul) by pressing soaked kokum petals.
Whisk kokum juice with fresh coconut milk.
Add crushed garlic, green chilli, roasted cumin powder, and salt.
Chill for 30 minutes, garnish with fresh coriander, and serve cold.

title: South American Baked Sweet Potato Wedges
description: Crispy baked sweet potato wedges tossed in paprika, cumin, and olive oil, serving as a nutrient-rich whole food starch.

instructions.text: Toss sweet potato wedges with olive oil, paprika, cumin, garlic powder, and sea salt.
Arrange in a single layer on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 25–30 minutes, flipping halfway through.
Serve crisp with homemade dip.

imageAttribution.title: South American Baked Sweet Potato Wedges
imageAttribution.creator: Unsplash

title: Spanish Garlic Mushrooms (Champiñones al Ajillo)
description: Sautéed button mushrooms infused with fragrant garlic, dry white grape juice/broth, parsley, and olive oil.

instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add sliced garlic and chilli flakes; sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add mushrooms and cook for 6–8 minutes until golden.
Pour in broth/lemon juice, cook off liquid, and sprinkle fresh parsley.

title: Spanish Gazpacho (Cold Tomato Soup)
description: A chilled Andalusian raw vegetable soup blended from ripe tomatoes, cucumbers, bell peppers, garlic, and extra virgin olive oil.

ingredients.name: sherry vinegar or red wine vinegar

instructions.text: Combine chopped tomatoes, cucumber, green bell pepper, garlic, olive oil, and vinegar in a high-speed blender.
Blend on high until completely smooth.
Season with salt and pepper, adding a splash of cold water if needed for desired consistency.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before serving in cold bowls.

title: Sprouted Moong Chaat
description: A fresh, tangy Indian snack of sprouted mung beans, cucumber, tomato, lime, and roasted cumin.

instructions.text: For food safety, steam or boil the mung sprouts for 5 minutes, then drain and cool. Keep them warm instead if serving as a warm chaat.
Combine sprouts, cucumber, tomatoes, onion, cilantro, and chilli in a bowl.
Add lemon juice, cumin powder, chaat masala, and salt. Toss well and taste for seasoning.
Serve promptly as a snack or light meal.

nutrition.micronutrientEstimateSource: Approximate per-serving estimates from generic cooked mung sprouts and raw vegetables; sprouting time, produce size, and seasoning blends vary.

title: Steamed Edamame with Sea Salt
description: Young green soybeans steamed in their pods and tossed with coarse sea salt, offering an effortless protein-rich plant snack.

ingredients.name: coarse sea salt or flaky salt

instructions.text: Bring water to a rapid boil in a pot.
Add frozen edamame pods and cook for 4–5 minutes until bright green and tender.
Drain well and transfer to a serving bowl.
Sprinkle coarse sea salt over pods while hot and serve immediately.

title: Steamed Fish with Ginger and Green Onions
description: Tender white fish fillet steamed with julienned ginger, green onions, and light soy sauce in traditional Cantonese style.

instructions.text: Place fish fillet on a heatproof plate; top generously with julienned ginger.
Steam over boiling water for 8–10 minutes until fish flakes easily.
Mix tamari, sesame oil, and water; pour over cooked fish.
Garnish with fresh julienned spring onions.

imageAttribution.title: Steamed Fish With Ginger And Green Onions
imageAttribution.creator: Unsplash

title: Tandoori Chicken with Vegetables
description: Oven-roasted yogurt-marinated chicken with warming tandoori spices, peppers, and red onion.

instructions.text: Score the chicken lightly. Mix yogurt, lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, tandoori masala, turmeric, oil, and salt.
Coat the chicken thoroughly and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes, or up to 8 hours.
Heat the oven to 220 degrees Celsius. Arrange chicken, pepper, and onion on a lined tray in a single layer.
Roast until the chicken is browned and the thickest pieces reach 74 degrees Celsius, about 25 to 35 minutes. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

nutrition.micronutrientEstimateSource: Approximate per-serving estimates from generic cooked chicken thigh, yogurt, and vegetables; chicken trim, marinade retention, and spice blends vary.

title: Tandoori Chicken
description: Chicken pieces coated in a spiced yogurt marinade, seasoned with garlic, ginger, lemon, and warm spices, baked or roasted.

instructions.text: Make deep slashes on chicken pieces.
Combine yogurt, ginger-garlic, lemon juice, spices, salt, and oil into a smooth marinade.
Marinate chicken for at least 2 hours (or overnight in the fridge).
Bake in a preheated oven at 200°C (400°F) for 25-30 minutes, turning once until tender.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and lemon juice.

title: Tandoori Pomfret
description: Whole pomfret fish marinated in a blend of yogurt, mustard oil, lemon juice, and aromatic Indian spices, then grilled.

instructions.text: Mix yogurt, spices, lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, and mustard oil to make a marinade.
Coat the scored pomfret evenly and marinate for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven/grill or pan-sear on a lightly greased skillet.
Grill/cook for 5-7 minutes on each side until cooked through and slightly charred.
Serve hot with lemon wedges and onion rings.

nutrition.micronutrientEstimateSource: Per-serving values from CTI_RECEIPES.pdf. Vitamin D converted from IU to mcg (1 mcg = 40 IU).

title: Tex-Mex Stuffed Bell Peppers
description: Halved bell peppers stuffed with black beans, brown rice, sweet corn, salsa, and melted low-fat cheese.

instructions.text: Pre-steam bell pepper halves for 5 minutes until slightly softened.
Mix brown rice, black beans, corn, salsa, cumin, and half the cheese.
Stuff pepper halves generously with rice-bean mixture.
Top with remaining cheese and bake at 190°C (375°F) for 20 minutes.

title: Thai Coconut Tom Yum Vegetable Soup
description: A fragrant Thai hot-and-sour soup simmered with lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime, mushrooms, and a touch of coconut milk.

instructions.text: Bring vegetable broth to a boil with lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in light coconut milk, chilli paste, and soy sauce; simmer gently for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat, stir in fresh lime juice, and serve warm.

imageAttribution.title: Thai Coconut Tom Yum Vegetable Soup
imageAttribution.creator: Unsplash

title: Thai Green Papaya Salad (Som Tum)
description: A tangy, crunchy Northeastern Thai salad made with shredded green papaya, cherry tomatoes, green beans, peanuts, and lime juice.

ingredients.name: long green beans, cut into 1-inch pieces

instructions.text: Pound garlic and red chilli in a mortar with a pestle.
Add long green beans and cherry tomatoes, bruising gently.
Add lime juice, soy sauce, and coconut sugar; mix well.
Add shredded green papaya and toss vigorously; sprinkle roasted peanuts before serving.

imageAttribution.title: Som Tam green papaya salad, Bangkok, Thailand
imageAttribution.creator: Vyacheslav Argenberg

title: Thalipeeth (Maharashtrian Multi-Grain Flatbread)
description: A wholesome Maharashtrian savory flatbread prepared from roasted multi-grain flour (bhajani) and onions.

ingredients.name: bhajani flour (roasted jowar, bajra, chana dal and rice flour)

instructions.text: Combine bhajani flour, chopped onions, coriander, sesame seeds, turmeric, chilli powder, and salt into a dough.
Pat a portion of dough directly onto a moist cloth or parchment paper to form a flat disk.
Make a small hole in the center and transfer onto a warm non-stick tawa.
Drizzle minimal oil and cook both sides on medium flame until crisp and golden brown.

title: Tofu and Vegetable Rice Paper Dumplings
description: Crispy pan-seared rice paper rolls packed with shredded cabbage, carrots, mushrooms, and firm tofu.

ingredients.name: water, warm, for soaking the wrappers

instructions.text: Sauté crumbled tofu, cabbage, carrots, and mushrooms with soy sauce for 5 minutes.
Soak rice paper wrapper in warm water; place filling in center and fold into a square packet.
Pan-sear dumplings in 1 tsp oil for 3 minutes per side until crispy.
Serve hot with soy dipping sauce.

imageAttribution.title: Tofu And Vegetable Rice Paper Dumplings
imageAttribution.creator: Unsplash

title: Tomato Omelette (Besan Chilla)
description: A savory pan-cooked pancake made from chickpea flour batter mixed with chopped tomatoes, onions, spices, and herbs.

instructions.text: Whisk besan with water to form a smooth, pourable batter.
Mix in tomatoes, onions, chillies, turmeric, ajwain, and salt.
Heat a non-stick skillet and grease lightly with oil.
Pour a ladle of batter, spread evenly in a circle, and cook on medium heat until golden.
Flip and cook the other side until done. Serve warm with mint chutney.

title: Turkish Lentil Soup (Mercimek Çorbası)
description: A silky, smooth red lentil soup infused with cumin, paprika, and a touch of lemon, popular across Anatolia.

instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a pot and sauté onion, carrot, and potato for 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and cumin powder, cooking for 1 minute.
Add rinsed red lentils and vegetable broth; bring to a boil.
Simmer for 20 minutes until lentils and veggies are soft, then blend until silky smooth.

title: Tuscan White Bean and Spinach Stew
description: A comforting Italian stew of creamy cannellini beans cooked with fresh spinach, garlic, tomatoes, and rosemary.

instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a pan; sauté garlic and rosemary for 1 minute.
Add diced tomatoes, white beans, and vegetable broth; simmer for 12 minutes.
Stir in fresh spinach and cook for 2 minutes until wilted.
Season with salt and black pepper and serve hot.

imageAttribution.title: Tuscan White Bean And Spinach Stew
imageAttribution.creator: Unsplash

title: Vegetable Moong Dal Khichdi
description: A comforting one-pot rice and mung dal meal with vegetables, turmeric, cumin, and ginger.

instructions.text: Rinse rice and moong dal together until the water runs mostly clear. Drain.
Heat ghee or oil in a heavy pot. Add cumin seeds and ginger; stir for 30 seconds, then add turmeric.
Add rice, dal, vegetables, water, and salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently, stirring occasionally, until the rice and dal are very soft.
Add a little hot water if a looser consistency is desired. Taste, adjust seasoning, and serve warm.

nutrition.micronutrientEstimateSource: Approximate per-serving estimates from generic rice, mung dal, and vegetable composition; rice variety and ghee or oil choice vary.

title: Vegetable Poha
description: A light Maharashtrian breakfast of flattened rice with peas, turmeric, peanuts, and fresh lime.

instructions.text: Rinse the poha briefly in a sieve, drain well, and leave it to soften for 8 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Heat the oil in a wide pan. Add mustard and cumin seeds; when they crackle, stir in the peanuts and cook until lightly toasted.
Add the onion, potato, peas, chilli, turmeric, and salt. Cover and cook over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until the potato is tender.
Fold in the softened poha and warm gently for 3 to 4 minutes. Turn off the heat, add lemon juice and cilantro, and serve warm.

nutrition.micronutrientEstimateSource: Approximate per-serving estimates from generic ingredient composition and stated quantities; brands, produce size, and salt use vary.

title: Vegetable Sambar
description: A tangy South Indian lentil stew with toor dal, drumstick, pumpkin, tomato, and tamarind.

instructions.text: Rinse the toor dal. Pressure-cook or simmer it with 500 ml water until very soft, then mash until creamy.
In a pot, simmer the drumstick, pumpkin, tomatoes, shallots, sambar powder, tamarind, salt, and remaining water until the vegetables are tender.
Stir the mashed dal into the vegetables. Add water to reach a stew-like consistency and simmer gently for 8 minutes.
Heat oil in a small pan. Add mustard seeds, dried chilli, and curry leaves; when fragrant, pour the tempering over the sambar and serve.

nutrition.micronutrientEstimateSource: Approximate per-serving estimates from generic pulse and vegetable composition; sambar powder, dal variety, and salt use vary.

title: Vietnamese Fresh Spring Rolls (Goi Cuon)
description: Translucent rice paper wraps stuffed with steamed shrimp, rice vermicelli, fresh mint, cilantro, and crisp lettuce.

ingredients.name: water, warm, for dipping the wrappers

instructions.text: Dip a rice paper wrapper in warm water for 5 seconds until pliable.
Lay wrapper flat; place lettuce, vermicelli, cucumber, carrot, mint, and cilantro on lower third.
Place 4 shrimp halves orange-side down above veggies.
Fold sides in, roll bottom firmly over filling, and roll up tightly.

title: Warm Roasted Beet and Walnut Salad
description: Warm oven-roasted beet cubes tossed with toasted walnuts, arugula, goat cheese, and balsamic vinaigrette.

instructions.text: Toss beet cubes in 1 tsp oil and roast at 200°C for 30 minutes.
Arrange arugula on a platter and top with warm roasted beets.
Sprinkle toasted walnuts and crumbled goat cheese.
Drizzle olive oil, balsamic vinegar, and salt.

imageAttribution.title: Warm Roasted Beet And Walnut Salad
imageAttribution.creator: Unsplash

title: West African Peanut and Tomato Stew (Light Version)
description: A rich West African vegetable stew infused with natural peanut butter, tomatoes, sweet potatoes, and spinach.

instructions.text: Sauté onion, garlic, and ginger in a pot with a drop of oil.
Add sweet potato, crushed tomatoes, and vegetable broth; simmer for 15 minutes.
Whisk peanut butter with warm broth until smooth and stir into pot.
Add spinach and cook for 3 minutes until wilted.
